Daily Excelsior 04:08 AM Oct 13, 2026 IST NEW DELHI, Oct 12 : Three districts -- Gaya in Bihar, Nagaur in Rajasthan and Umaria in Madhya Pradesh -- have been recognised as the best-performing aspirational districts in transforming the agriculture sector in the first year of implementation of the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY). The three districts are among the 100 aspirational districts chosen under the scheme on the basis of three indicators: low crop productivity, low cropping intensity and low agricultural credit disbursement. In addition, 18 districts were recognised for exemplary work across the scheme's six key objectives: For enhancing agricultural productivity (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Maharashtra), Chitrakoot (UP), Gyalshing (Sikkim); crop diversification and sustainable practices (Mahoba (UP), Dindori (MP), Chamoli (Uttarakhand). Advertisement Post-harvest storage capacity (Tikamgarh (MP), Sidhi (MP), Dantewada (Chhattisgarh); irrigation infrastructure (Kishtwar (J&K), Dahod (Gujarat), Chhota Udepur (Gujarat); access to short- and long-term agricultural credit (Narayanpet (Telangana), Jalaun (UP), Sri Sathya Sai (Andhra Pradesh); and governance and service delivery (Nagarkurnool (Telangana), Kachchh (Gujarat), Haveri (Karnataka). Backed by an estimated annual outlay of Rs 24,000 crore, the PM-DDKY integrates 36 central schemes across 11 ministries and departments, besides state programmes and private sector partnerships. Marking the completion of the scheme's first year, Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said, "The first year had focused on establishing strong foundations, while the coming year must be dedicated to delivering visible and measurable outcomes on the ground." He stressed the need to improve productivity, increase cropping intensity, strengthen irrigation and water management, facilitate access to credit, promote high-value agriculture, improve post-harvest infrastructure and enhance farmers' incomes. The ultimate measure of the scheme's success, Chouhan said, would be the difference it makes to farmers' lives. He urged all stakeholders to strengthen coordination, speed up implementation and focus on measurable gains in agricultural outcomes and sustainable farm incomes. "The coming year will focus on scaling up successful interventions and improving outcomes across all identified districts, with the overarching vision of making all 100 PMDDKY districts truly 'Dhan-Dhaanya' - rich in grain and rich in prosperity," he said. Chouhan reaffirmed the Centre's commitment to working with state governments, district administrations, scientific institutions and farmers to translate district action plans into tangible results. The minister also spoke about the Khet Bachao Abhiyan, to be held across all states from October 22 to November 30, 2026, which aims to promote soil health through balanced and judicious use of fertilisers. Bihar’s Energy Minister highlighted the Bihar Green Hydrogen Policy, 2026 , which seeks to promote green hydrogen production, attract investment and create employment opportunities in the state. Key Points Production Target: The policy aims to establish an annual green hydrogen production capacity of 1 lakh tonnes within five years. Investment and Incentives: The state government expects to attract approximately ₹16,000 crore in investment. Employment Generation: The policy is expected to create more than 12,000 direct and indirect jobs. Green Hydrogen Green hydrogen is produced by splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen through electrolysis using renewable electricity. It can help decarbonise hard-to-abate sectors such as steel, fertilisers, oil refining and heavy transport, while strengthening energy security by reducing dependence on fossil fuel imports. However, its large-scale adoption requires adequate renewable energy, water resources, efficient electrolysers, storage facilities and transportation infrastructure. In this context, the National Green Hydrogen Mission aims to establish India as a global hub for green hydrogen production, utilisation and export, with targets of achieving at least 5 million metric tonnes (MMT) of annual production capacity, adding approximately 125 GW of renewable energy capacity, reducing annual greenhouse gas emissions by nearly 50 MMT. national_raw_news.title: 33 mins ago | National 12 Centre caps trade margins on anti-cancer drugs at 30% of MRP
national_raw_news.content: The Centre has informed the Supreme Court that it has decided to regulate trade margins on anti-cancer medicines by capping them at 30 per cent of the maximum retail price (MRP), while the apex court called for a broader review of medicine pricing across the pharmaceutical sector. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Union government, told a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta that the Centre would notify a list of cancer drugs to which the trade margin cap would apply. The Centre’s second highest law officer submitted that the list could be periodically updated to include additional anti-cancer medicines, depending on market developments and public health considerations, while excluding inexpensive drugs. The development came after the apex court repeatedly questioned the substantial disparity between the price at which medicines are supplied to retailers and the MRP printed on them, raising concerns over the financial burden on patients and the need for an effective regulatory framework. However, the Justice Vikram Nath-led Bench questioned whether the proposed measure would address the wider problem of excessive trade margins on medicines and medical devices beyond the anti-cancer segment. During the hearing, the top court cited the example of an Indian-made cardiac stent supplied to retailers at around 5,000 rupees but carrying an MRP of 25,000 rupees and questioned the justification for such a disparity. SG Mehta responded that stents were already subject to price caps. The apex court has now posted the matter for further hearing on October 27.

Daily Excelsior 04:19 AM Oct 13, 2026 IST MP Gulam Ali Khatana along with Director PIB, Neha Jalali inaugurating Multimedia Exhibition at Katra on Monday. Excelsior Correspondent KATRA, Oct 12: Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, Gulam Ali Khatana inaugurated an eight-day multimedia exhibition organized by the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), J&K, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, at the Government Higher Secondary School premises in Katra in the presence of Director of CBC and PIB Jammu, Neha Jalali, Sub-Divisional Magistrate (Katra), Piyush Dhotra, and other officials. The outreach drive, themed "12 Saal-Vishwas Ke, Vikas Ke, Jan Kalyan Ke", coincides with the ongoing Navratra festival at Katra that witnesses lakhs of devotees every year to pay obeisance at the revered shrine. Advertisement The inaugural ceremony also focused on themes like Reform Utsav and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan. Speaking on the occasion, Gulam Ali Khatana highlighted the significant reforms and transformative initiatives undertaken by the Narendra Modi-led Government over the past 12 years, aimed at strengthening the Indian economy, promoting inclusive development and improving the quality of life of citizens. He said that the Government has taken several important steps to simplify business processes, promote ease of doing business, encourage entrepreneurship and create new opportunities for the youth. Khatana observed that the multimedia exhibition would serve as an effective medium for generating awareness about the welfare schemes and development initiatives of the Modi Government. Through informative displays, audio-visual presentations and other communication materials, the exhibition can help people understand the objectives, benefits and implementation of various Government programmes, he underlined. While appreciating the efforts of CBC in effectively disseminating information of GoI schemes, Khatana urged the CBC officials to organise more such exhibitions in remote areas to strengthen public outreach at the grassroot level. Expressing concern over the harmful impact of drugs, the MP called for focused awareness activities to educate people, especially youth, about the physical, psychological and social consequences of substance abuse. Earlier, Neha Jalali outlined the aims and objectives of various awareness initiatives of the Department, stating that last-mile communication remains critical to ensuring that benefits under Central Welfare Schemes reach intended beneficiaries. She briefed about various key welfare initiatives and structural reforms introduced over the past 12 years across sectors such as financial inclusion, women empowerment, healthcare, and rural infrastructure.
